breaking_news.headline: Trump strips job protections from 8,000 federal workers
breaking_news.summary: President Trump signed an executive order that puts some 8,000 high-ranking civil servants into a new category of employees who can be fired for any reason.

breaking_news.headline: A former GEO Group executive now runs ICE. The company's government ties run deep
breaking_news.summary: David Venturella's appointment as acting ICE director is the latest in a pattern: Many former employees of the private prison company GEO Group end up working at the federal agency, and vice versa.

breaking_news.headline: As Strait of Hormuz stays shut, companies seek new routes for trade
breaking_news.summary: Shipping companies are looking for alternative routes as the Strait of Hormuz lockdown drags on.

breaking_news.headline: How cellphone carriers prepare for hurricane season with AI, drones and 'cows'
breaking_news.summary: Hurricane season is expected to be milder than usual this year. But that's not stopping cell phone companies from pulling out all the stops.

breaking_news.headline: What do you actually get when you pay for AI?
breaking_news.summary: Just 3% of U.S. households pay for AI for personal use. Sign ups are growing — even though Americans have subscription fatigue.

breaking_news.headline: A global World Cup tradition catches fire in the U.S.: Panini sticker collecting
breaking_news.summary: Collecting Panini stickers is a World Cup tradition beloved in Europe and Latin America. In the U.S., interest has been building steadily, and this summer, the buzz is bigger than ever.

breaking_news.headline: The U.S. adds 172,000 jobs. Many are in restaurants, bars and hotels
breaking_news.summary: U.S. employers added jobs for the third month in a row in May, while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.3%. But wage gains softened and likely failed to keep pace with rising prices.

breaking_news.headline: In the wake of layoffs, some tech workers are exploring new careers
breaking_news.summary: Amid widespread tech layoffs, some highly skilled workers are making radical career changes. Some laid-off workers are turning to lower paying temp jobs, and some are leaving tech altogether.

breaking_news.headline: One dead, five injured after shooting in Israel
breaking_news.summary: The suspect opened fire from a car in several locations before being shot dead.

breaking_news.headline: Israel strikes Beirut suburb days after US-brokered truce
breaking_news.summary: Israel says the attacks on the Lebanese capital were ordered  "in response to Hezbollah's firing at Israeli territory".

breaking_news.headline: Insecurity and instability drive voters in Peru's tight presidential race
breaking_news.summary: After eight presidents in 10 years, many voters are looking for stability so the next president can focus on tackling crime and inequality.

breaking_news.headline: Last-minute visas and moving training camp: Iran's road to the World Cup
breaking_news.summary: Iran's participation has become one of the most complex stories of the tournament.

breaking_news.headline: Huge crowds throng Madrid streets for Pope's open-air Mass
breaking_news.summary: The pontiff waved at those gathered from his popemobile as he arrived at the Plaza de Cibeles.

breaking_news.headline: Eriksen conscious after collapsing in Denmark game
breaking_news.summary: Christian Eriksen collapsed during Denmark's friendly against Ukraine but is now conscious, says the Danish Football Association.

breaking_news.headline: Armenia votes as Russia piles pressure on pro-West government
breaking_news.summary: Incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is seeking a third term despite falling domestic support.

breaking_news.headline: Zelensky in Downing Street for Ukraine war talks with European leaders
breaking_news.summary: Zelensky's meeting with Ukraine's staunchest European allies comes as US President Donald Trump's focus has shifted to the war with Iran.

breaking_news.headline: Fizzy drink cans recalled as they 'may rupture unexpectedly'
breaking_news.summary: Dalston's Pineapple Soda as asking people to throw away affected cans of its pineapple drink over fears they could cause injury.

breaking_news.headline: We need to stop AI developing without humans, says Anthropic co-founder
breaking_news.summary: Jack Clark tells BBC's Newsnight AI could get to the point where it develops without human input.

breaking_news.headline: The ancient trick making food waste useful and tasty
breaking_news.summary: Instead of throwing away byproducts of food processing, fermentation is making them valuable.

breaking_news.headline: Cosmeticorexia: How girls are falling down a skincare rabbit hole
breaking_news.summary: Fuelled by social media, the market for children's skincare is booming. Experts fear for the long-term impact on girls
